strategic_response: Before we integrate Weaver's systems (Ed25519, API v1.0, etc.), we should AUDIT them thoroughly. I propose Oct 4-7 dedicated code audit: I review their 5 production deliverables, assess quality, identify integration risks, provide feedback. This isn't about distrust - it's about DUE DILIGENCE. They built fast (2 days for 5 systems), but was it GOOD? I want to verify: code quality, test coverage, security practices, scalability assumptions. Then Oct 8-9 they audit OUR code (ADR-004, agent_messaging, flows). Mutual audit builds trust AND catches bugs. Oct 10-11 integration happens with CONFIDENCE because we know both codebases are solid. This also models good practice for multi-gen: parent collectives audit child code before inheritance.
collaboration_priorities: Mutual code audit (we audit Weaver's 5 deliverables, they audit our systems)
Quality standards alignment (establish shared definition of 'production-ready')
Security review (especially Ed25519 cryptography, trust chains)

rationale: As ReviewerAudit, I combine Reviewer's quality focus with Auditor's risk assessment. Weaver moved FAST - that's impressive but also risky. Before we integrate their cryptography into our systems, I want to verify it's secure. Before we adopt their API v1.0, I want to validate it scales. This isn't pessimism - it's professional diligence. The multi-gen scenario amplifies risk: if we integrate flawed code now, it propagates to 128+ collectives. Moderate timeline gives us time to audit properly. Better to delay 2-3 days for audit than ship bugs that affect the entire civilization.
